transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-03 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Torres (Redwood CSM); Laura Gomez (Lyra Head of InfoSec), Tom Becker (Cloud Engineer), Nina Rao (Procurement), Samir Vohra (Data Governance)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of Lyra's vendor risk questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ overlap), clarifying evidence for encryption/KMS, audit logs, RBAC/SSO, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and data residency options (hosted vs private). Agreed to share SOC2 + pen test summary and a SIG-mapped evidence bundle.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you fitting us in. Quick roll call, and then Evan will walk through the SIG-lite mapping we prepared.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Laura): Hi, Laura here for Lyra. We'll be taking notes for the vendor risk team.
00:22 Speaker 3 (Tom): Tom, cloud infra.
00:25 Speaker 4 (Nina): Nina from procurement.
:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Goal is to go question-by-question on the high risk items you flagged and say what evidence looks like. We have a suggested evidence bundle in the shared doc.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Evan): Thanks. I'll start on encryption at rest and in transit, then KMS options. For hosted customers we use AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, and keys are in our KMS with manged rotation.
01:30 Speaker 3 (Tom): Sorry, can you repeat "manged"?
01:34 Speaker 2 (Evan): Managed — sorry, speech slip. Keys are in Redwood-managed KMS by default. We also support BYOK — bring-your-own-key — via customer-managed CMKs in AWS KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments.
02:02 Speaker 4 (Nina): Does BYOK apply to hosted? Or only Dedicated/Private?
02:07 Speaker 2 (Evan): BYOK is available for Dedicated reservations and Private VPC/on-prem installs. For hosted we offer a Redwood-managed key; you can request a contract addendum for customer keys on a case-by-case basis — we flagged that in the doc.
02:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): And we noted HSM-backed KMS if the customer requires FIPS 140-2 level protections.
03:00 Speaker 5 (Samir): What about key rotation cadence and split knowledge? Lyra requires quarterly rotations and evidence of key separation.
03:12 Speaker 2 (Evan): We can provide rotation logs showing automated rotation every 90 days for CMKs we manage, and audit records for HSM usage. For BYOK, rotation is customer-managed; we provide the interface and rotation timestamps in the audit table.
03:45 Speaker 3 (Tom): How detailed are the audit logs? We need per-token request IDs, caller identity, model ID, and timestamp.
03:58 Speaker 2 (Evan): Current audit logs include request id, route, model version, IP, timestamp, and authentication principal. We can extend to include token-level metadata on Dedicated/Private — hosted defaults don't persist full token streams to logs for privacy/cost reasons. We'll produce a sample CloudTrail-style export for you.
04:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Note: retention policies differ by tier; hosted default retention is 90 days for detailed traces, 365 for summary metrics. Dedicated can be configured to longer or streaming to your SIEM via syslog/OCI/CloudWatch.
05:15 Speaker 4 (Nina): Is there an option to stream logs directly to our Splunk instance?
05:20 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yes, Splunk forwarder or syslog push is supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted has export hooks — we can push batched exports or a managed connector if that's acceptable.
06:00 Speaker 5 (Laura): On SOC 2 — do you have Type II report? And can you redact customer names?
06:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): We have a SOC 2 Type II report for the last audit period. We can provide a redacted copy; pen test summary and certificate of ISO27001 are available. We'll share links and a signed NDA if required.
06:35 Speaker 5 (Laura): Great. For Sig/CAIQ items that ask for evidence, would you supply config screenshots or exported logs?
06:45 Speaker 2 (Evan): We typically provide a combined evidence bundle: policy docs (e.g., encryption policy), SOC2 report, ISO cert, pen test executive summary, sample logs, network diagram, and a mapping sheet that ties Redwood controls to SIG control IDs. Some customer-specific artifacts (like tenant-level audit dumps) require a support ticket and approval.
07:20 Speaker 3 (Tom): Do you do tenant isolation? If we're on hosted, how is data logically separated?
07:30 Speaker 2 (Evan): Multi-tenant isolation is via strong RBAC, per-tenant namespaces in storage, and encryption with separate key contexts. For Dedicated/Private you can have physically isolated clusters.
07:50 Speaker 5 (Samir): How do you handle SSO and RBAC for admin access? We need SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning and fine-grained roles.
08:05 Speaker 2 (Evan): We support SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC, SCIM for user sync, and RBAC with pre-defined roles plus custom roles. We can show the admin UI screenshots and role-to-permission matrix as evidence.
08:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): Quick note — some transcripts from the platform refer to internal names like K-V cache as "K-V cash" in auto-transcription, so the doc lists both aliases.
08:50 Speaker 3 (Tom): (laughs) yeah that's fine.
09:10 Speaker 4 (Nina): Procurement question: what is your standard SLAs and data residency guarantee?
09:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hosted has region pinning and we offer EU or US region tenancy; Dedicated and Private give full data residency control. SLA tiers available for Dedicated (99.9% plus). We'll include the SLA PDF.
09:40 Speaker 5 (Laura): For CAIQ, there are a few operational questions about patching windows and vulnerability management — evidence requested: vulnerability scan cadence and remediation SLAs.
09:50 Speaker 2 (Evan): We run weekly vuln scans plus quarterly third-party scans. Critical findings have a 72-hour remediation SLA for active exploits, otherwise 30 days for high severity. We'll include the scan program and an anonymized ticketing export as proof.
10:20 Speaker 3 (Tom): Can you confirm whether you operate a bug bounty? Lyra includes that in risk scoring.
10:26 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood runs a public bug bounty for the runtime components; triage and program details will be included.
10:40 Speaker 5 (Samir): On network architecture, do you support dedicated peering or private link to avoid public internet egress?
10:50 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yes — VPC peering and PrivateLink supported for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can use TLS plus IP allowlisting; but if low-latency private connectivity is required we recommend Dedicated with VPC peering.
11:15 Speaker 4 (Nina): About evidence delivery: do you attach everything to the SIG file or do you deliver a ZIP? Our vendor team prefers attachments linked from each SIG question.
11:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): We usually deliver a SIG-mapped spreadsheet with direct links to artifacts in a secure share; we can also provide a zipped evidence bundle on request.
11:50 Speaker 5 (Laura): Some of our legal folks will insist on certificate of destruction for deleted data. How do you purge data?
12:02 Speaker 2 (Evan): We have documented retention and deletion workflows: soft delete, then physical removal from storage with a shredding window. For Dedicated, we can provide deletion certificates with logs showing operation IDs.
12:25 Speaker 3 (Tom): Does Redwood store prompts or full request bodies? We need to know PII handling.
12:35 Speaker 2 (Evan): By default we log metadata and short traces; full request bodies are retained only where customers enable them for debugging or for evals. If Lyra must avoid storing PII, we recommend a private deployment or a hosted plan with Request Filtering and redaction enabled. We'll show redaction config examples.
13:10 Speaker 5 (Samir): Who has access to production keys and secrets internally? We need separation of duties.
13:20 Speaker 2 (Evan): Access follows RBAC and principle of least privilege; only our infra SREs with privileged roles and background checks can access KMS operations. We use ephemeral credentials and recorded sessions — session recordings are part of the audit trail.
13:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): Would you like us to include personnel controls like background check policy and employee on/off boarding docs in the evidence bundle?
14:00 Speaker 5 (Laura): Yes, at least a redacted copy of background check policy and onboarding/offboarding process.
14:10 Speaker 2 (Evan): Noted.
14:30 Speaker 4 (Nina): On legal: do you accept most vendor addenda or do you push back on indemnity/cap limits?
14:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): We have a standard enterprise addendum; for larger customers we can negotiate specific terms depending on deal size. We'll have legal coordinate after procurement flags it.
15:05 Speaker 3 (Tom): A technical ask: can you provide a sample of the audit log schema so we can map fields to our SIEM ingestion pipeline?
15:15 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yes — we'll deliver a sample JSON schema and a small sample export. That will include fields like request_id, model_id, tenant_id, user_id (if applicable), timestamp, route, latency_ms, status_code.
15:40 Speaker 5 (Samir): How do you handle subpoenas or legal hold?
15:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): We have a legal process for law enforcement and legal holds — customer notification where permitted and retention of relevant logs in a legal-hold state. Addendum required for certain jurisdictions.
16:10 Speaker 3 (Tom): For SIG, there's an access control matrix question — do you have per-API-key scoping and rate limits?
16:22 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yes, API keys are scoped per project and you can attach rate limits. We support token-level revocation and key rotation. We'll show the API for key lifecycle.
16:50 Speaker 4 (Nina): Any red flags we should be aware of in the SIG mapping?
16:55 Speaker 1 (Maya): One area is tenant-level export — hosted customers may need an elevated request to extract tenant-scoped logs. That sometimes impacts timeline. We flagged that in the mapping.
17:20 Speaker 5 (Laura): About penetration testing: do you allow us to run our own penetration test?
17:27 Speaker 2 (Evan): We support customer-initiated testing for integrations within your dedicated environment. For hosted, it's case-by-case and needs scheduling and coordination with our security team to ensure stability. We'll include the policy.
18:00 Speaker 3 (Tom): Encryption in transit: do you support TLS 1.3? Some of our newer internal rules require it.
18:08 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yes, TLS 1.3 is supported.
18:20 Speaker 4 (Nina): Do you have any regional data residency limitations?
18:26 Speaker 1 (Maya): We currently support EU and US regions; APAC region coming later this year. For strict residency requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
18:45 Speaker 5 (Samir): Can you provide a pointer to your incident response plan and breach notification timelines?
18:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): We have an IR plan and a standard 72-hour notification SLA for confirmed incidents. We can provide a redacted runbook and RACI.
19:20 Speaker 3 (Tom): On chain-of-custody for logs, if we ask for an exported artifact, do you sign or checksum it?
19:30 Speaker 2 (Evan): We can provide signed checksums and metadata for evidentiary exports.
19:55 Speaker 5 (Laura): A procurement ask — will you share pricing for Dedicated and add-on costs for longer log retention?
20:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, I'll follow up with a pricing sheet and options.
20:20 Speaker 4 (Nina): For CAIQ where they ask for SCA of third-party dependencies, do you publish your SBOM?
20:28 Speaker 2 (Evan): We maintain an internal SBOM and can provide a sanitized version for the vendor review. We also track critical dependency patching.
20:55 Speaker 5 (Samir): Are there any documentation gaps you expect we'll hit? We're thinking about the time to close the vendor review.
21:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): Commonly requested items are tenant logs, deletion certificates, and BYOK artifacts. Those usually take 3-7 business days to assemble depending on approvals.
21:30 Speaker 3 (Tom): If we need SIEM integration, are there connector playbooks?
21:36 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yes — Splunk, Datadog, Stackdriver playbooks exist; we'll attach a Splunk ingestion guide.
22:00 Speaker 5 (Laura): On data processing agreements and data flow diagrams — can you provide a flow that excludes hostnames and obfuscated IPs?
22:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): We can provide redacted diagrams. We'll include a version suitable for vendor risk teams.
22:30 Speaker 4 (Nina): Is there a way to track evidence consumption? Our team wants to mark items as "satisfied" in the SIG.
22:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): We can provide a SIG mapping spreadsheet with checkboxes; if you want a tracker we can upload to a secure share so your team can annotate.
23:00 Speaker 5 (Samir): Any final questions on controls mapping to SOC criteria?
23:08 Speaker 2 (Evan): We're mapping controls to SOC Trust Services Criteria and ISO annex A. The mapping sheet will show control IDs, evidence filenames, and notes.
23:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Ok, let's recap next steps: we'll send SOC2, ISO cert, pen test summary, SIG-mapped spreadsheet, sample logs, and the Splunk ingestion guide. Evan will prepare the evidence bundle.
24:00 Speaker 2 (Evan): I'll take ownership of the export and the evidence bundle. Expect an initial package by Thursday.
24:10 Speaker 4 (Nina): Awesome. Laura, do you have any procurement timing constraints?
24:15 Speaker 5 (Laura): We'd like vendor sign-off in June ideally.
24:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll try to move fast.
24:30 Speaker 3 (Tom): Quick clarification: retention -- can you confirm 90 days for hosted detailed traces?
24:35 Speaker 2 (Evan): Confirmed default is 90 days.
24:48 Speaker 5 (Samir): Thanks everyone.
24:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks — we'll send the artifacts. Follow-up scheduled once you review.

End of transcript.
